template.title: Cayley graph of degree {d} and diameter {k}
template.statement: Find a group G and a generating set S of G, closed under inverses and without the identity, with |S| <= {d}, such that the Cayley graph Cay(G, S) has diameter at most {k}, with as many vertices |G| as possible.
template.submission: Text file: either 'points m', then the generators as permutations of 0..m-1, one per line (the images of 0, 1, ..., m - 1), or 'semidirect m n a' (the group Z_m x|_a Z_n of the table, [x, y][u, v] = [x + u mod m, y a^u + v mod n]), then the generators as pairs 'x y', one per line; see checkers/cayley_check.py.

score: the number of vertices, the order of G (larger is better)
best_text: The largest known Cayley graph in the Combinatorics Wiki's table has {best} vertices ({holder}); a Cayley graph with more vertices improves it.
holder_unknown: not named in the table's colour key
holder_sources: the colour of the entry in the wiki's table and the page's colour key; for a raised value, Comellas's entry or the paper
open_rule: every entry of the table (degree 3 to 20, diameter 2 to 10) not in bold (bold entries are optimal) and not proven optimal since, with at most 10,000,000 vertices; the best known value is the largest of the wiki's, Comellas's Cayley graphs and the papers in literature.json
left_out: 21 optimal (bold), 2 proven optimal since (Macaj 2026), 35 more than 10,000,000 vertices
